summary: A burning coal holds fire and can kindle another material. The woman of Tekoa turns that familiar property into a picture of the last life that can carry on a family.

senses.definition: The high priest carries coals from the altar in a censer. In David’s song fire from Yahweh kindles coals, and glowing coals accompany the storm.

senses.gloss: last surviving member of a family
senses.definition: The woman of Tekoa calls her surviving son her one remaining ember. Extinguishing it would leave her husband without a name or remnant.
The proverb tells the hearer to give food and water to an enemy, describing the result as heaping coals upon his head. Paul takes up the saying in his appeal to overcome evil with good.

note: The Greek connection in Romans is a quotation of Proverbs. Neither passage states precisely what the recipient experiences in the image of coals on the head.
